summary: Retry a peer's exchange as soon as its route answers a probe after an outage, instead of up to 30 seconds after the failure. An exchange that got no response head (refused, closed, reset or aborted before an answer) and whose route then answers a HEAD probe is retried at that probe. That early attempt is spent until a probe sees the route down again or an exchange succeeds, so each early attempt costs one export, signature and exchange per observed outage and recovery of a peer's route. A peer that answered and failed, or stalled after connecting, keeps the 30-second cap

replay.detail: No replay or rebuild; only the local retry timing of the replication worker changes.

schema.detail: No tables, columns, indexes or triggers; the spent state is in memory per worker.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: No wire, authentication or client change; members on any build interoperate, and the retry timing is local.

downtime.detail: A daemon restart to install the build; no extra interruption.

recovery.detail: Swap back to the previous binary freely; nothing new is persisted.
